strings.name: Olga Tokarczuk
strings.summary: Trained in psychology, Tokarczuk uses travel, myth and multiple perspectives to examine identity and coexistence. Primeval and Other Times explores Polish history; Flights uses fragments to consider movement and the body; The Books of Jacob reconstructs a world across religions. Her narratives bring humans, animals and local memory into relation. She won the 2018 International Booker and received the 2018 Nobel Prize in Literature in 2019.

strings.influence.rationale: Explored borders, history and identity in works including Flights and The Books of Jacob, expanding the international reach of Polish literature.
strings.facts.fact-01.label: Birthplace
strings.facts.fact-02.label: Education
strings.facts.fact-02.value: Graduated in psychology from the University of Warsaw in 1985
strings.highlights.highlight-01.title: A novel of travel in fragments
strings.highlights.highlight-01.text: Flights juxtaposes journeys, bodies and historical stories; Tokarczuk shared the 2018 International Booker with translator Jennifer Croft.
strings.highlights.highlight-02.title: History across cultures
strings.highlights.highlight-02.text: The Books of Jacob revisits the eighteenth century through multiple identities and faiths, continuing her exploration of borders and perspectives.
strings.timeline.event-01.title: Publishes Świata jest za dużo
strings.timeline.event-01.text: The Polish novel centers on postwar displacement and rebuilding lives in Lower Silesia, continuing her exploration of history’s effects on individuals.
strings.timeline.event-02.title: Publishes The Empusium
strings.timeline.event-02.text: Set in a health resort before the First World War, the novel examines European cultural traditions through gender prejudice and unease.
strings.timeline.event-03.title: Receives the 2018 Nobel Prize
strings.timeline.event-03.text: The delayed award recognized her boundary-crossing narrative imagination; the award year and announcement year are distinct.
strings.timeline.event-04.title: Flights wins the International Booker
strings.timeline.event-04.text: She shared the prize with Jennifer Croft, bringing her fragmented narratives of travel and bodies to wider international readers.
strings.timeline.event-05.title: Publishes The Books of Jacob
strings.timeline.event-05.text: Multiple witnesses reconstruct the world of Jacob Frank, exploring histories of shifting religion, language and identity.
strings.timeline.event-06.title: Publishes Flights
strings.timeline.event-06.text: Interlinked fragments examine movement, anatomy and the wish to preserve bodies, extending the structure of the conventional novel.
strings.timeline.event-07.title: Publishes Primeval and Other Times
strings.timeline.event-07.text: A fictional village and successive generations reflect twentieth-century Polish history in a major early breakthrough.
strings.timeline.event-08.title: Publishes her first novel
strings.timeline.event-08.text: The Journey of the Book-People appeared after her psychology training and professional work, marking a turn toward literary life.
strings.timeline.event-09.title: Born in Sulechów
strings.timeline.event-09.text: Born in Poland, she later studied psychology in Warsaw; concerns with minds and social boundaries continued into her writing.
